items.front: Calorie norm anchoring India's traditional poverty line?
items.back: 2400 kcal/day rural and 2100 kcal/day urban per person.
items.examPoint: Poverty line — concept & calorie norm (2400 rural / 2100 urban kcal)

items.front: HCR vs Poverty Gap Index — what does each measure?
items.back: HCR = incidence (share of people below the line); Poverty Gap = depth (average income shortfall).
items.examPoint: Absolute vs relative poverty; Head Count Ratio & poverty gap

items.front: Four poverty-estimation committees in order (with years)?
items.examPoint: Alagh Committee/Task Force (1979) — first calorie-based line

items.back: Tendulkar (MRP) 21.9%; Rangarajan (MMRP, costlier basket) 29.5% — govt didn't officially adopt Rangarajan.
OPHI (Oxford) + UNDP; 3 dimensions, 10 indicators; Alkire-Foster counting method.
items.examPoint: Global MPI — OPHI & UNDP, Alkire-Foster, 3 dimensions/10 indicators

items.front: How does India's National MPI differ from the Global MPI?
items.back: Same 3 dimensions but 12 indicators — adds Maternal Health and Bank Accounts (uses NFHS data).

items.front: NITI Aayog's 2023 national MPI headcount trend?
items.examPoint: National MPI findings — 24.82 crore escaped; 29.17% to 11.28%

items.front: Define disguised unemployment and its link to the Lewis model.
items.back: Surplus workers with near-zero marginal productivity (typical of farms); Lewis moves them to industry without cutting output.
Structural (skill mismatch), Frictional (job transition), Cyclical (recession), Seasonal (off-season).

items.front: PLFS — when launched, what it replaced?
items.back: Launched 2017 by NSO (MoSPI); replaced the NSSO's quinquennial Employment-Unemployment Surveys.
items.examPoint: PLFS — launched 2017, replaced NSSO quinquennial EUS

items.front: PLFS reference periods: UPS vs CWS vs CDS?
items.back: UPS = 365 days; CWS = 7 days (≥1 hr any day = employed); CDS = each day of the week (intensity).
Monthly labour-force estimates for both rural and urban areas (larger sample, calendar-year basis).
100 days wage work/rural household (1/3 women, ABPS from 2024); repealed by the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025.
